summary: Time-window skew between edge and control plane causing 429s during priority-weight promotion
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reported a wave of 429 responses immediately after their orchestrator increased request priority (background -> interactive) across ~300 workers in prod-us-west. The Console shows token credit available at the tenant level, but the edge logs return 429s for a subset of connections for ~45–90s after the promotion.

Impact:
- ~8% of interactive requests from BrightCart received 429s for ~1.5 minutes after their priority-weight promotion.
- Latency and user-facing errors were reported in their checkout A/B test impacting conversion for the window.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (BrightCart dedicated lease) in prod-us-west.
- Priority promotion performed by their orchestration service (staggered rollout to 300 worker pods over 30s).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start with sustained background ingestion at 120 requests/s.
2) Trigger priority-weight promotion to interactive across all workers (orchestrator calls admin API that flips priority flag).
3) Workers immediately begin sending interactive requests at previous throughput, client-side backoff disabled for quick recovery.
4) Observe a spike of 429s reported by the client for some connections for up to ~90s.

Observed behavior:
- 429 responses from edge instances with headers: X-RateLimit-Window=60s, X-RateLimit-Remaining varying by connection.
- Console tenant token balance shows available credits and no global cap reached.
- Edge metrics show a short-lived token-debit spike and a mismatch between edge-local refill ticks and control-plane refill epoch.

Expected behavior:
- Priority promotion should not cause tenant-level 429s when tenant has available credits; edge should coordinate refill/weight update with control plane to avoid double-debit or early rejections.

Customer ask:
- Immediate mitigation or configuration guidance to prevent 429s when promoting many workers' priority within a short window.
steps_to_reproduce: Start with background traffic at 120 rps from orchestrator workers
Call admin API to set priority=interactive for all workers within ~30s window
Observe client logs / telemetry for 429s and Console quota readout
logs: [edge-03] 2026-03-14T15:02:12Z WARN quota: token-debit failed tenant=brightcart amount=1 window=60s remaining=0
[cp-sync] 2026-03-14T15:02:13Z INFO sync: applied-priority-update tenant=brightcart plan=dedicated ttl=18s
comments: Sara Patel (Support) 2026-03-14: Customer reports 8% of interactive requests returned 429s after bulk priority change. They're asking for a short-term workaround and an explanation.
BrightCart-SRE (customer) 2026-03-14: We promoted ~300 pods over 30s. We saw 429s for ~45-90s; our quota UI still showed credits available. We can stagger promotions if recommended.
Ethan Kim (Support/Eng) 2026-03-14: Assigned. I'll pull edge and control-plane metrics for the window and check refill epoch alignment. Can you share the orchestrator rollout timestamps?
BrightCart-SRE 2026-03-14: Shared rollout timestamps and worker IDs in private attachment (log bundle).

Ethan Kim (Eng) 2026-03-14: Initial hypothesis: edge-local refill ticker is out-of-sync with control plane post-priority-update causing transient negative remaining on some edge nodes. Investigating rate-limiter logs and CP sync traces.
investigation_notes: Checked control-plane quota ledger: tenant credit remained positive and consistent across cp replicas.
Edge instances report refill granularity of 30s while control plane uses 60s epoch for refill; several edges had last tick ~30s older than CP tick at time of promotion.

Token-debit logic: on promotion, edge applies new priority weight immediately and debits token buckets based on new weight before CP refill tick arrives — this can momentarily exhaust edge-local bucket even though CP shows available credits.
Observed that orchestrator promot-es were all within a narrow window; many edges attempted larger per-request debits simultaneously, amplifying the transient exhaustion.
No evidence of global quota exhaustion or billing-related truncation.
Relevant artifacts: edge rate-limiter traces (edges 03/07/12), cp-sync logs, Grafana dashboard snapshot (quota-debits-per-edge-2026-03-14-15).
short_term_mitigation: Advice provided to customer: stagger priority promotions across a longer window (recommended 10–20s per 50 workers) and enable client exponential backoff for immediate retries.

Support action: disabled eager priority-apply toggle for BrightCart's dedicated pool for the next 2 hours (temporary control-plane config) to allow edges to reconcile ticks before applying heavier debits.
CS notified customer about temporary toggle and monitoring in place.
Engineering temporary check: deploy a config that enforces a soft-delay (3s) on applying increased weights at edge after control-plane ack.
resolution_notes: Hotfix merged: add a 2–4s guarded window before edge applies new priority weight when a control-plane priority update is detected (PR https://github.com/redwood/release/pull/4512).
Edge refill ticker alignment improved: introduced a sync handshake so edges request next refill epoch timestamp during cp-sync to avoid 30s vs 60s skews.

Deployed hotfix to prod-us-west dedicated pool in a staggered rollout at 2026-03-14T18:40Z. Post-deploy monitoring shows no repeat 429 waves during a synthetic priority promotion test (3 experiments).
Follow-up INT task created to add a Canary test for priority promotions and to update runbook: INT-3312.
Customer BrightCart confirmed reduction of 429s in their next rollout and accepted stagger recommendation as an operational best practice.
Permanent fix timeline: full control-plane/edge refactor scheduled in Q2 2026 to centralize refill epoch enforcement across regions.
Ticket to remain open until post-mortem and runbook updates are published.
follow_up_actions: INT-3312: Add canary and e2e test for priority promotion path (assigned to Runtime team).
Update public docs / Console guidance: add recommended rollout cadence when changing priority-weight at scale.
Notify Customer Success to proactively advise dedicated customers on safe promotion patterns.
Monitor BrightCart metrics for next 72 hours and confirm stability.
